note: All data below is fictional / illustrative, built for the ApexSignal technical assignment. Company names are real for realism; relationship states, quotes, and events are invented.

nodes.name: Iberdrola
nodes.description: Spanish multinational utility. Client of this assessment. ~180 TWh generated annually, heavy renewables build-out across Iberia, UK, US, and Brazil.

nodes.name: Spanish Ministry for Ecological Transition
nodes.description: Sets renewable auction schedules and grid permitting timelines that directly gate Iberdrola's Spanish pipeline.

nodes.name: UK Dept. for Energy Security & Net Zero
nodes.description: Ongoing dispute over offshore wind Contracts for Difference strike-price levels; Iberdrola has paused two UK final investment decisions pending the next auction round.

nodes.name: US Department of Energy
nodes.description: Federal tax-credit guidance for offshore wind (Avangrid assets) remains unsettled, creating financing uncertainty.

nodes.name: Brazilian Ministry of Mines and Energy
nodes.description: Supportive of Neoenergia's distribution expansion; recent tariff review favored cost recovery.

nodes.name: Basque Regional Government
nodes.description: Home region of Iberdrola's headquarters; generally cooperative on industrial policy and green hydrogen incentives.

nodes.name: CNMC (Spanish energy regulator)
nodes.description: Sets allowed returns on regulated grid assets. Current review cycle keeps WACC roughly flat, a mild negative versus Iberdrola's ask.

nodes.name: Ofgem
nodes.description: RIIO price control settlement for ScottishPower networks came in below Iberdrola's requested capex allowance.

nodes.name: FERC
nodes.description: Reviewing interconnection queue reform that affects Avangrid's transmission projects in the Northeast.

nodes.name: ANEEL
nodes.description: Brazilian electricity regulator; latest distribution tariff cycle was constructive for Neoenergia.

nodes.name: European Commission (DG ENER)
nodes.description: REPowerEU and grid-investment frameworks broadly favor Iberdrola's electrification thesis.

nodes.name: ScottishPower (subsidiary)
nodes.description: Wholly owned UK subsidiary; fully integrated into group strategy.

nodes.name: Avangrid (subsidiary)
nodes.description: US subsidiary; NYSE-listed minority float adds governance visibility but not much friction.

nodes.name: Neoenergia (subsidiary)
nodes.description: Brazilian subsidiary; minority listed on B3. Currently the group's fastest-growing regulated base.

nodes.name: Masdar (offshore wind JV partner)
nodes.description: Co-investor in East Anglia offshore wind assets; relationship has deepened with a second joint project announced this year.

nodes.name: Endesa
nodes.description: Largest domestic rival for Spanish renewable auction capacity; direct competitor in same CNMC proceedings.

nodes.name: Naturgy
nodes.description: Competes for the same grid connection points in northern Spain; occasional co-bidder in international tenders.

nodes.name: EDP
nodes.description: Iberian rival, particularly in hydro and cross-border interconnection capacity.

nodes.name: RWE
nodes.description: Competes head-to-head in UK and US offshore wind auctions.

nodes.name: Ørsted
nodes.description: Both firms are bidding aggressively into the same depressed US offshore wind tax-credit environment, and industry pricing pressure is mutual.

nodes.name: Siemens Gamesa
nodes.description: Primary offshore turbine supplier; recent blade reliability issues have delayed two UK projects and strained the contract.

nodes.name: Vestas
nodes.description: Secondary onshore turbine supplier, increasingly favored after the Siemens Gamesa reliability issues.

nodes.name: ArcelorMittal
nodes.description: Steel supplier for transmission towers and foundations.

nodes.name: Prysmian
nodes.description: Subsea and grid cabling supplier for offshore interconnections.

nodes.name: Microsoft (PPA offtaker)
nodes.description: Long-term renewable power purchase agreement backing US data-center demand; recently expanded.

nodes.name: Amazon (PPA offtaker)
nodes.description: Corporate PPA counterparty for US wind capacity.

nodes.name: Spanish Industrial Consumers Association
nodes.description: Large industrial users lobbying publicly for lower regulated tariffs, putting pressure on Iberdrola's grid revenue assumptions.

nodes.name: European Investment Bank
nodes.description: Provides concessional financing for grid modernization projects.

nodes.name: BlackRock
nodes.description: Among the largest institutional shareholders; historically a stable, low-friction holder.

nodes.name: Norges Bank Investment Management
nodes.description: Large sovereign-wealth shareholder with an active ESG engagement track record.

nodes.name: Banco Santander
nodes.description: Lead relationship bank for Iberian project financing and hedging.

nodes.name: CCOO (industrial union)
nodes.description: In active negotiation over headcount at a legacy thermal plant slated for closure.

nodes.name: UGT (industrial union)
nodes.description: Co-party to the same thermal-closure negotiation; historically more conciliatory than CCOO.

nodes.name: Greenpeace Spain
nodes.description: Generally supportive of Iberdrola's renewables build-out but publicly critical of remaining gas-plant capacity.

nodes.name: ClientEarth
nodes.description: Has threatened litigation over the permitting pathway for a contested onshore wind corridor in northern Spain.

nodes.name: Chair, CNMC Energy Division
nodes.description: Career regulator seen as a swing vote on the pending WACC review.

nodes.name: UK Minister for Energy Security
nodes.description: Publicly signaled impatience with developer demands in the CfD process ahead of the next auction round.
